title: Copilot tops GitHub's own AI code review benchmark. An independent one tells a different story.
key_facts: GitHub unveiled ReviewBench, an open benchmark developed with Microsoft for AI code review tools; it used 219 public pull requests from 187 repositories in 19 languages.
GitHub Copilot code review leads the initial leaderboard with a 40.1% grounded F1 score.
GitHub ran the first tests itself using publicly available products; vendors did not run or verify them, and tests were run on different dates (Copilot on 1 Oct, Cubic and Greptile in June).
On Martian's independent online leaderboard (6 Oct) Cubic is first with 64.9% F1 and Copilot fourth with 60.9%.
On Martian's offline leaderboard Qodo Deep ranks first and Copilot fifth with a 58% F2 score.
The New Stack says the scores are not directly comparable because the datasets and methods differ.
quote_evidence: A vendor-published benchmark topped by that vendor’s own product makes those qualifications particularly notable.
These scores still aren’t directly comparable with ReviewBench.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows how the choice of benchmark can change which AI code reviewer looks best.
event_date: 5 Oct 2026 (GitHub announced "on Monday"); our 6 Oct edition carried the launch
notes: Follow-up: our 6 Oct 2026 edition carried GitHub's ReviewBench announcement; new today is the independent comparison with Martian's leaderboards.
